oem.faqSub: The practical points that decide an OEM feasibility check.
oem.o1: What is the OEM minimum order quantity?
oem.oa1: Minimum quantities depend on product line, size, grit mix and packaging; they are confirmed in the feasibility review that comes back with your quotation.
oem.o2: What artwork do you need from us?
oem.oa2: Print-ready artwork with your brand, the label sizes you use, and any destination marks required. Artwork requirements are confirmed in the review before a run.
oem.o3: Can I get a sample run before committing?
oem.oa3: Yes. Samples of standard references are available for evaluation, and OEM artwork approvals follow the confirmed specification.
oem.o4: Do you pack under our brand only?
oem.oa4: Yes. Private label runs apply your logo, labels, sizes and packaging; labels are applied and verified before the carton is sealed, not after it lands.
oem.o5: How long does an OEM feasibility check take?
oem.oa5: The check follows the review step; stock references are answered fastest because no converting lead time applies to them.

coltBuy.guideSub: Four points that decide which product fits your application — confirm them with the quotation.
coltBuy.specSub: What the line covers today, straight from the product records.
coltBuy.faqTitle: Questions buyers ask about this line
coltBuy.belts[0].q: Which belt width suits my machine?
coltBuy.belts[0].a: The documented sizes run from 533 × 75 mm to 2200 × 1330 mm; ultra-wide single-piece belts above 1500 mm avoid a joint. State the machine, load and finish so the width is confirmed with the quotation.
coltBuy.belts[1].q: What grit range can I order?
coltBuy.belts[1].a: Grits 40–800 across aluminium oxide, zirconia and silicon carbide grain. Coarse grit removes stock quickly; fine grit blends and finishes.
coltBuy.belts[2].a: Yes. Width and length beyond the documented sizes are quoted case by case; converting to a custom size affects both lead time and minimum order quantity.
coltBuy.belts[3].a: Joint type and edge treatment are specified per reference. Tell us the machine, load and speed so the right construction is confirmed.
coltBuy.discs[0].q: Hook & loop, PSA or mesh — which for my tool?
coltBuy.discs[0].a: Hook & loop suits frequent grit changes on a random-orbit sander, PSA suits flat pads and long run times, and mesh suits dust extraction.
coltBuy.discs[1].q: What sizes and hole patterns are documented?
coltBuy.discs[1].a: 3, 4, 5 and 6-inch discs with the hole patterns of each reference; the arbor or centre hole must match your tool.
coltBuy.discs[2].a: Coarse grit removes rust and paint quickly; fine grit blends and prepares for finishing. State the material and the finish required.
coltBuy.discs[3].a: Mesh and perforated dustless formats are documented in this line; the perforated pattern keeps the surface visible while sanding.
coltBuy.flap[0].a: Plastic suits general metal grinding, steel suits demanding deburring and fiberglass suits high-speed durability; the arbor hole must match the tool.
coltBuy.flap[1].q: What are flap discs used for?
coltBuy.flap[1].a: Grinding welds, removing rust, blending surfaces and finishing metal parts — matched to the tool's rated speed with the guard fitted.
coltBuy.flap[2].a: Yes. Flap discs are supplied in bulk for distributors and workshops; grit, backing, diameter and quantity are set together in the quotation.
coltBuy.flap[3].q: Why does my disc glaze on mill scale?
coltBuy.flap[3].a: Mill scale loads the abrasive quickly. Choose a coarser grit, keep the disc flat to the work and dress the surface as it loads.
coltBuy.all[0].q: Where do I start if my application is not listed?
coltBuy.all[0].a: Send the material, machine, finish and volume; we reply with the product family, specification and lead time that fit.
coltBuy.all[1].q: Can I order one of each reference first?
coltBuy.all[1].a: Samples of standard references are available on request; sample availability and freight terms are confirmed with your reply.
coltBuy.all[2].q: Do you quote OEM across all lines?
coltBuy.all[2].a: Yes. Logo, labels, sizes and packaging are quoted against a feasibility review across belts, discs and flap discs.
coltBuy.all[3].q: Where do the sanding sponges sit in the range?
coltBuy.all[3].a: Hand sanding: flexible pads for curves and profiles, foam blocks for flat surfaces and repaired walls. Both are quoted with dimensions, grit, foam density and quantity.
coltBuy.sponge[0].q: Flexible pads or foam blocks — which for my job?
coltBuy.sponge[0].a: Flexible pads suit curves, edges and profiles; foam blocks suit flat surfaces, edges and repaired walls. Both are reusable after cleaning.
coltBuy.sponge[1].q: Does the foam colour indicate grit?
coltBuy.sponge[1].a: No. Foam colour is not a grit or hardness rating. Confirm grit, abrasive material and foam density in your enquiry and we match it in the quotation.
coltBuy.sponge[2].q: Can you die-cut custom shapes and pack under my brand?
coltBuy.sponge[2].a: Yes. Send your profile, thickness, grit, packaging format and target quantities; die-cutting tooling and artwork requirements are confirmed in the review.
coltBuy.sponge[3].a: They can be rinsed and reused until the abrasive layer is spent; lifetime depends on grit, pressure and the surface worked.
spongePage.gritNote: Foam colours do not establish grit or hardness. Confirm dimensions, grit, abrasive material, foam density, packaging and quantity in your enquiry.

spongePage.a2b: Sanding blocks for smoothing drywall joints, feathering joint compound, and preparing walls for primer and paint.
spongePage.a3b: Flexible, reusable abrasive sponges for wet or dry sanding. The foam conforms to curves, edges, and profiles for controlled hand sanding.
spongePage.q1: Does the colour identify the abrasive type?
